findings.claim: The newly admitted other + text/* source files are run through stripPreviewText, a Markdown/HTML-clip sanitizer, so the excerpt on a source file's card is not the file's first lines but a mangled version of them.
findings.impact: In normal use, a folder of C, JS, CSS, Python, Perl or XML files shows card excerpts that silently differ from the file content. `#include <stdio.h>` shows as `#include `. Any `<` ... `>` pair is deleted even across lines, so `for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n  p->x = 1;` becomes `for (i = 0; i x = 1;`, and the same happens to JS arrow functions after a comparison. `/* Reset */` in CSS/C becomes `/ Reset /`. `char *a, *b;` becomes `char a, b;`. Python `def f(*args, **kw)` loses its stars. The `#` of a `# comment` line is stripped, and `fns[i](x)` collapses to `fnsi`. A `.xml`/`.sgm`/`.sgml` file (other + text/xml, text/x-sgml, also admitted by the text/* prefix) loses every tag and can show a blank excerpt (title only), which looks the same as having no excerpt. behavior.md's stated user-visible result is that the card 'shows its first lines'.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/textExcerpt.ts:17-18 admits every file_type other with a text/* mime. frontend/src/components/TextThumbnail.tsx:69-83 sends every non-Office file to stripPreviewText. frontend/src/components/TextThumbnail.tsx:41 `.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, "")` ([^>] also matches newlines), :42 `^#+ ` strip, :44 link-collapse `\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]*\)`, :47-48 `**x**`/`*x*` strips. backend/app/services/filetype.py:136-188 maps .bat/.c/.h/.ksh/.pl to text/plain, .py to text/x-python, .css to text/css, .js/.mjs to text/javascript, .xml to text/xml, .sgm/.sgml to text/x-sgml, .vcf to text/x-vcard and .n3 to text/n3, all as `other`. These were blank cards at origin/develop, so this commit is what first shows the mangled text for them. The R-5 record (docs/process/reviews/fix-source-card-excerpt/decisions.md:25-27) quotes only a Python file whose first lines contain none of these patterns.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariants file is declared. The defect is a silently wrong result in normal use for files the single user owns, not crafted input. The sanitizer is pre-existing, but this diff is what routes source files through it.

findings.proposed_fix: For a non-Markdown text mime (anything other than text/markdown or a clip), show the raw window without stripPreviewText's Markdown/HTML transforms, and add a test that renders TextThumbnail for a `.c`/`.css` file with a mocked Range response and checks the drawn text.

behavior.md's table does not cover file_type `subtitle` (text/vtt). The code says no excerpt, and no test pins it (F2).
Non-UTF-8 source files (for example Shift_JIS .c) are decoded as UTF-8 by res.text() and show replacement characters. The same already happens for .txt, but the number of affected file types grows.
regression_risks: officeMimes.test.ts no longer lists FileCard, FileListRow and JustifiedFileCell as OFFICE_MIMES importers. If a component reverts to an inline gate without the Office branch, that test no longer catches it, though sourceCardExcerpt's docx/xlsx/pptx rows would.

Any existing or future test that renders FileCard/FileListRow/FileGrid with an other + text/* fixture now mounts TextThumbnail, which calls `new IntersectionObserver` and needs a stub in jsdom. I found no such fixture today.
Lazy Range fetches to /stream now fire for every visible source-file card. The size is bounded at 1 KiB (TextThumbnail.tsx:17, files.py:842-881).
test_coverage: sourceCardExcerpt.test.tsx runs 26 rows across FileCard, FileListRow and JustifiedFileCell via FileGrid. With 19 measurable photos plus 1 file, the ratio is 0.95, at or above JUSTIFY_THRESHOLD 0.9 (listMeta.ts:22,61), so the justified branch really is exercised.
The test asserts only whether a text-thumbnail node exists, never its text. Mangled excerpt content (F1) is untested.
No subtitle row, so an allowlist-to-denylist mutation survives (F2).
Mutations of the shared helper (dropping the other branch, dropping the hasThumbnail guard, dropping the document guard on OOXML, dropping the null-mime guard) are each killed by at least one row.
